sentences.text: The Saint Helena rail was an extinct flightless rail native to the island of Saint Helena.
This bird was relatively large, reaching almost the size of the New Zealand weka.
Unlike the New Zealand weka, the Saint Helena rail had a more slender build.
The species possessed strong toes with long claws that allowed it to climb and flutter up steep valley walls.
It likely fed on the eggs and juveniles of various Saint Helena bird species as well as snails.
The species was described by American ornithologist Alexander Wetmore in 1963 from subfossil remains found in Prosperous Bay.
Paleontologist Storrs Olson suggested that the rail may have scavenged food dropped by visiting seabirds.
The species became extinct after 1502 due to introduced alien predators such as cats and rats.
In 1973, paleontologist Storrs Olson synonymized the genus Aphanocrex with the genus Atlantisia.
Current belief that the two species evolved separately has led to the species being reclassified into the monotypic genus Aphanocrex.
The species disappeared from Saint Helena in the early 16th century.
The genus lived from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, approximately 0.129 to 0 million years ago.
It is debated whether the Saint Helena rail is closely related to the Inaccessible Island rail, leading some scientists to retain it in the genus Aphanocrex rather than Atlantisia.
